# Graph-orbit compression of Baikov logarithmic sources

Date: 2026-08-30

Status: bounded RustRed research proposal, not a closure result

## Question and verdict

Can exact graph automorphisms compress the Baikov logarithmic-vector-field sources before
elimination, while preserving a universal all-rank reduction for the `K = 21` six-loop vacuum
family?

The answer has two parts.

1. **Yes, as a certificate-preserving storage, task-orbit, and equivariant-block technique.** A
   decorated graph automorphism can propose a loop-momentum map. After exact authentication, that
   map acts on the `L^2` ordinary vacuum sources and on every translated source identity. One may
   store orbit seeds, solve only canonical *tasks*, lazily generate orbit images, and block a
   genuinely invariant elimination problem.
2. **No, as a reason to keep only one equation from each orbit.** At `L` loops the constant source
   space still has dimension `L^2`. For the maximally symmetric `S_(L+1)` vacuum proxy, one source
   seed has an orbit spanning the entire source space, but the orbit contains more than `L^2`
   rows. Source-formula storage falls; the independent row rank does not. A useful K21 gain must
   therefore come from quotienting complete decorated tasks or lowering sparse-elimination fill,
   not from claiming that 36 sources have become one equation.

This is a promising bounded experiment at `K = 6`. It is not yet a preferred six-loop closure
architecture. The experiment must retain an exact uncompressed fallback and must be killed if the
gain disappears on boundary, guard, cut, or asymmetrically decorated cells.

## Published facts used here

### Complete low-degree Baikov sources

Boehm et al. derive logarithmic vector fields along the Baikov Gram determinant and prove that
their displayed set generates the relevant logarithmic-vector-field module. The generators have
degree at most one. For `L` loops and `E` independent external momenta their closed-form set has
`L(L+E)` members; a vacuum therefore has `q = L^2` members. The construction remains valid with
massive propagators because masses enter only after the linear change from scalar products to
Baikov variables.

Source:
[Boehm et al., arXiv:1712.09737](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09737), especially Sections IV--V.

That completeness theorem concerns the module of dimension-preserving Baikov vector fields. It
does **not** prove that a finite collection of descending symbolic rules closes every index ray.
The latter still requires translated equations, boundary owners, guard coverage, lower-sector
feedback, termination, and a finite terminal complement.

### Symmetry in existing reduction methods

Reduze 2 obtains physical-sector symmetries from graph automorphisms and same-mass multi-edge
permutations, then derives the associated loop-momentum shifts. It also retains a separate
combinatorial method because graph methods do not cover every abstract sector relation.

Source:
[von Manteuffel and Studerus, arXiv:1201.4330](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.4330),
Section 3.3.

Pak's alpha-representation canonicalization compares the `U` and `F` polynomials under line
permutations. It is a strong integral-family identification technique, but it is not a proof that
one row from an IBP-source orbit spans the other rows.

Source: [Pak, arXiv:1111.0868](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.0868), Section 2.

LiteRed uses equivalent-sector maps and internal sector symmetries alongside, rather than in place
of, its symbolic-rule search. Its rule search explicitly refines exceptional index domains after
generic rules fail.

Sources:

- [Lee, arXiv:1212.2685](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2685)
- [Lee, arXiv:1310.1145](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1145), Section 4

The 2026 seedless construction uses a numerator symmetry to order two ISP exponents, but still
needs separate boundary lowering operators when an exponent reaches zero. This is direct evidence
that a bulk symmetry quotient does not remove boundary completion.

Source:
[de la Cruz and Kosower, arXiv:2602.22111](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22111),
Sections III.1--III.2.

The 2026 generating-function algorithm says that globally related sectors need only one
representative generating function. In its equal-mass sunset discussion, however, global symmetry
lowers the master count separately from the IBP-only analysis. This distinction is exactly the one
RustRed must preserve: authenticated symmetry routes augment the IBP ideal; they are not silently
assumed to be generated by it.

Source:
[Feng et al., arXiv:2605.09541](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09541),
Sections 2.1 and 4.1.

### Massive spanning cuts are not an uncut closure certificate

NeatIBP 1.1 reports consistency failures when cut systems are formed by truncating equations and
then merged. The authors observe that diagrams with massive propagators are more prone to this
problem. The cut-local IBPs can still be valid; the inference from the collection of cut systems to
the uncut reduction is what must be checked.

Source:
[Wu et al., arXiv:2502.20778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20778), Section 3.2.

For RustRed's equal-mass vacuum lane, cuts may guide discovery and reduce a matrix. They cannot
authenticate closure. Every accepted rule must replay against the uncut exact family sources, and
every cut stitch must pass the uncut normal-form checks.

## Exact source action

Let

```text
O_i^j = partial / partial(l_i) dot l_j,       1 <= i,j <= L.
```

For an authenticated unimodular loop change `l = A k`, the source transforms as

```text
O_i^j -> sum_(a,b) (A^-1)_(a,i) A_(j,b) O_a^b.
```

Equivalently, a coefficient matrix `M` of a vector field transforms by conjugation,
`M -> A^-1 M A`, up to the chosen row/column convention. This has an important consequence:
ordinary source labels `(i,j)` are generally **not permuted**. A graph symmetry can map one matrix
unit to a linear combination of matrix units.

Therefore RustRed must distinguish three counts:

- **raw source count:** `q = L^2`;
- **orbit-template seed count:** how many source matrices are needed so that their exact group
  orbits span the source space;
- **independent source rank:** the rank of those orbit images, which remains at most and generically
  equal to `L^2`.

Keeping one literal `O_i^j` for every apparent label orbit is valid only when every authenticated
`A` is a signed permutation in the selected loop basis. Otherwise it deletes source directions.

## Quantitative source-orbit envelopes

### Maximally symmetric complete-family proxy

Take the `L+1` parallel-edge banana, or equivalently its `S_(L+1)` cycle-space action in the basis
`e_i - e_0`. Exact integer enumeration of the permutation group, conjugation orbit of `E_11`, and
rational row rank gives the following RustRed-side result.

| family | loops | raw sources | group | orbit seeds | orbit rows | exact span rank |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `K = 6` | 3 | 9 | `S4`, 24 | 1 | 12 | 9 |
| `K = 10` | 4 | 16 | `S5`, 120 | 1 | 20 | 16 |
| `K = 15` | 5 | 25 | `S6`, 720 | 1 | 30 | 25 |
| `K = 21` | 6 | 36 | `S7`, 5,040 | 1 | 42 | 36 |

These numbers are not a literature claim. They are an exact finite-group calculation proposed as
the first implementation test. It is readily replayed by constructing every `A_sigma`, applying
`A_sigma^-1 E_11 A_sigma`, deduplicating integer matrices, and taking exact rank.

For `L >= 3`, the conjugation representation on `End(V)` for the standard `S_(L+1)` module splits
over the rationals into dimensions

```text
1, L, (L+1)(L-2)/2, L(L-1)/2.
```

At `L = 6` these are `1 + 6 + 14 + 15 = 36`. An invariant orbit sum reaches only the trivial
one-dimensional component. Retaining invariant rows alone would discard 35 source directions.
The possible gain is an equivariant block solve across all four components, not an invariant-only
solve.

The table is deliberately adversarial: one seed expands to 42 rows at K21 before a 36-row basis is
selected. It gives a 36-to-1 formula-template reduction but no base row-rank reduction.

### Literal label-orbit envelope

If, and only if, the authenticated loop maps act by simultaneous signed permutations so that
matrix units remain matrix units, Burnside counting gives these ordered-pair orbit counts.

| loops | trivial | cyclic `C_L` | dihedral `D_L` | full `S_L` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3 | 9 | 3 | 2 | 2 |
| 4 | 16 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
| 5 | 25 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| 6 | 36 | 6 | 4 | 2 |

This table must not be applied to a general unimodular routing. For that case, RustRed must compute
orbit-span ranks in the linear representation rather than count label orbits.

### What to expect on physical six-loop sectors

There is no defensible universal number below 36 before the physical topology manifest is
decorated and enumerated. The bounds are:

```text
1 <= orbit-template seeds <= 36,
independent source rank <= 36.
```

The lower seed bound is attained by the full `S7` proxy above. A topology or cell with trivial
decorated stabilizer needs all 36 templates. A 15-propagator/six-ISP trivalent sector normally has
far less symmetry than the complete `K = 21` coordinate family, and dots, numerator powers, cuts,
and guards reduce it further. The experiment must report the actual weighted histogram of
stabilizer orders and source-seed counts. A topology-only group size is not a performance estimate.

## Where quotienting is safe

The following operations preserve the proof boundary.

1. Build a **decorated** graph whose equality data include masses, edge kind, direction where
   relevant, cut membership, and every restriction used to define the task.
2. Use each graph automorphism only to propose a loop-momentum map. Authenticate the map with the
   existing exact scalar-product and denominator replay. Require the correct unit Jacobian.
3. Construct the exact source representation from `A^-1 M A`, and verify the transformed Baikov
   polynomial vector field by exact sparse-polynomial equality.
4. Canonicalize a whole target task under any authenticated map that transports its target,
   complete domain, guards, ordering, and child-owner routes. Solve the canonical representative
   and transport the resulting rule back exactly.
5. Inside one fixed-target elimination, use only the subgroup that stabilizes all of those data.
   Store orbit seeds lazily, but materialize every independent source component needed by the
   exact row-space certificate.
6. If modular representation blocks are used, choose primes not dividing the stabilizer order.
   Reconstruct over the exact characteristic-zero coefficient field and replay there.
7. Canonicalize terminal values only through exact integral routes. Store the normalization and any
   mass or Jacobian factor explicitly.

For an equal-mass unit-scale family, an automorphism may freely exchange edges with the same mass
tag. Setting `m^2 = 1` does not erase the need for the tag: it distinguishes a massive edge from a
massless edge and is part of the proof-relevant graph color.

## Where stabilizers, guards, and rank break the quotient

### Domain stabilizers

A group mapping one RuleCell to another can canonicalize the *whole task*. It cannot delete rows
inside a fixed-cell solve. That solve may use only

```text
H = Stab(target, sector, cut, cell, guards, ordering, lower owners).
```

Generic cells often have trivial `H`. Stabilizers can jump on equality faces such as `n1 = n2`, so
the group must be recomputed per exact stratum. RustRed already has the right conservative pattern:
`residual_stabilizers` retains a denominator permutation only when it preserves the cell base.
The new lane must extend that check to guard ideals and source representations, not bypass it.

Relevant local implementation:

```text
crates/rustred-core/src/foundry/cell/projection.rs:503
```

### Guard strata

If a rule divides by `p(n,d)`, a symmetry sends the guard to `g.p`. It is unsafe to use the rule on
the full orbit unless one of the following is proved:

- the guard ideal and nonzero branch are invariant under `H`;
- every transformed guard branch has its own exact owner; or
- the transported rule is retained with its transformed guard.

Special equality strata can both enlarge a stabilizer and make a leading coefficient vanish. They
must be refined before quotienting. Averaging rules can introduce a coefficient whose zero locus is
larger than the original loci, creating new exceptional rays.

### Arbitrary numerator rank

An all-rank symmetry route is cheap only when the complete scalar-product coordinates are
permuted. With a general linear ISP map, a degree-`r` monomial in `s` ISP variables can expand into
as many as

```text
binomial(r + s - 1, s - 1)
```

monomials. For the six ISPs of a trivalent six-loop family, this bound is 3,003 at rank 10,
53,130 at rank 20, and 1,221,759 at rank 40. A fixed expansion cap is therefore a discovery limit,
not an all-rank certificate.

The production route should prefer an auxiliary coordinate basis permuted by the authenticated
group. If no such basis exists, it must transport generic index-polynomial rules without expanding
a concrete rank, or fall back to the uncompressed source lane. Failure to find a permutation basis
does not permit a rank cutoff.

### Cuts

For cut set `C`, only `Stab(C)` acts within the cut problem. A full-family automorphism generally
moves one cut to another. That is useful for canonicalizing cut tasks, but not for replacing the
uncut proof. Massive cut systems receive an additional rule: no merged cut result is accepted until
its uncut source replay and uncut path-consistency checks pass.

### Nonminimal universal terminals

A finite nonminimal terminal set is allowed, but symmetry does not prove that it is finite or
universal. Those properties still come from exact all-stratum closure. Once finiteness is proved:

- ship either a union of complete terminal orbits or one representative plus an exact route for
  every omitted member;
- do not replace a nontrivial terminal representation by orbit sums alone;
- if a terminal maps to a linear combination rather than one integral, retain the exact basis map;
- validate numerical terminal values after all routing and normalization factors; and
- measure epsilon-pole debt on the routed reductions. Symmetry does not lower the required Laurent
  depth automatically.

The relaxed nonminimal policy helps only after the closure complement is finite and the resulting
orbit-representative evaluation table remains affordable.

## Symbolica boundary

### Supplied graph primitives

Symbolica re-exports Graphica as `symbolica::graph` at:

```text
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/lib.rs:177
```

The vendored Graphica implementation supplies:

- `Graph::canonize()` using McKay canonical labeling;
- explicit vertex maps and automorphism generators in `CanonicalForm`;
- exact colored-graph isomorphism through `Graph::is_isomorphic()`; and
- an automorphism group size that also counts identical parallel-edge permutations.

Relevant source locations:

```text
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/lib/graphica/src/lib.rs:619
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/lib/graphica/src/lib.rs:1367
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/lib/graphica/src/lib.rs:1383
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/lib/graphica/src/lib.rs:1777
```

Two cautions are proof-critical.

1. `automorphism_group_size` includes identical-edge permutations, but a group-size factor is not
   an explicit loop-momentum map. RustRed must derive and authenticate every map it uses.
2. `HiddenData<T,U>` excludes `U` from equality and hashing. Mass, cut, routing, and guard colors
   must never be placed in its hidden component.

The second behavior is defined at:

```text
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/lib/graphica/src/lib.rs:122
```

### Supplied sparse-polynomial primitives

`MultivariatePolynomial` stores sparse terms with a dense exponent vector per term and supports
variable unification, reordering, coefficient maps, derivatives, and polynomial substitution.

Relevant source locations:

```text
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:286
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:605
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:1408
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:1453
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:1608
FOR_REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_PUSH/symbolica/src/poly/polynomial.rs:1938
```

These primitives are sufficient for exact Baikov-polynomial construction, differentiation, and
source-action replay. RustRed should add only a bounded **simultaneous** linear-substitution
adapter.
Sequential calls to `replace_with_poly` can alias old and new variables and implement the wrong
map; fresh temporary variables or a term-wise homomorphic image avoids that error.

### RustRed-owned proof machinery

Symbolica does not turn a graph automorphism into RustRed's complete certificate. RustRed must own:

- cycle-basis and loop-map derivation;
- exact momentum, denominator, mass, cut, and Jacobian authentication;
- the `L^2` source representation and orbit-span certificate;
- decorated task and guard stabilizers;
- sparse modular row selection and exact reconstruction;
- strict-descent, overlap, finite-complement, and terminal certificates; and
- resource-bounded lazy orbit materialization.

The current exact authentication boundary is already suitable:

```text
crates/rustred-core/src/sector/symmetry/mod.rs:1
```

The current `Canonicalizer` stores the full closure of authenticated denominator permutations. It
does not represent general linear actions on source matrices or numerator polynomials:

```text
crates/rustred-core/src/sector/symmetry/canonical/action.rs:13
```

K6 already authenticates two integer momentum maps generating the order-24 `S4` edge action:

```text
crates/rustred-core/src/foundry/artifact/three_loop/symmetry.rs:12
```

That makes K6 the correct first experiment; no new topology-authored trust shortcut is needed.

## Concrete RustRed experiment

### Data model

Add an experimental, non-production owner with approximately these semantics:

```text
AuthenticatedOrbitGroup
  family_fingerprint
  decorated_graph_fingerprint
  generator_routes[]
    vertex permutation
    exact loop matrix A and inverse
    exact denominator permutation or linear action
    exact source action M -> A^-1 M A

SourceOrbitCertificate
  subgroup fingerprint
  ordered seed matrices[]
  lazy orbit routes[]
  selected independent image routes[]
  modular scout ranks[]
  exact characteristic-zero span replay

StableEliminationTask
  target and ordering
  sector/cut/cell fingerprint
  guard-ideal fingerprint
  immutable child-owner fingerprints
  exact stabilizer subgroup
```

Store only generator matrices and compact group routes. At S7, storing 5,040 dense `36 x 36`
source-action matrices would waste several tens of megabytes before coefficient overhead. Compose
the `6 x 6` loop action along a cached route and construct source images lazily.

### Pipeline

1. Construct a fully colored Symbolica graph and canonize it.
2. Derive candidate cycle-space maps from explicit vertex generators.
3. Authenticate every generator through RustRed's existing exact family-map verifier.
4. Build the source representation by conjugation and replay it against the Symbolica Baikov
   polynomial.
5. For each exact task, compute its full decorated stabilizer.
6. Greedily discover orbit seeds over two finite-field primes, but keep all rank-increasing images.
7. Reconstruct the selected span over the exact coefficient field and prove that it contains every
   original ordinary source used by the uncompressed baseline.
8. Compare two solvers:
   - lazy orbit generation with ordinary sparse elimination; and
   - stabilizer-equivariant block elimination using all required representation components.
9. Lift every candidate rule exactly, replay the original uncompressed sources, and run the normal
   RuleCell closure, guard, overlap, descent, and terminal checks.
10. Reduce the same symbolic rays with compressed and uncompressed artifacts. Require identical
    exact terminal normal forms, not merely equal modular ranks.

The modular stage is discovery only. The source-span proof, rule identities, and closure artifact
are exact characteristic-zero certificates.

### Parallelism and I/O

The immutable authenticated group and orbit certificates should be shared across workers. Workers
own only their current sparse elimination frontier and exact-lift candidates. Orbit images are
generated on demand into bounded caches keyed by `(task, source seed, group route, translation)`.
No worker should clone the complete group of source polynomials. Checkpoints record compact routes
and pivots rather than expanded orbit rows.

## Kill gates

### K6: correctness and value test

Use the existing K4/Mercedes `K = 6` family and all five registered three-loop graph classes.

1. Reproduce the exact `S4` order 24 from the two authenticated generators.
2. Reproduce `12` distinct images and exact rank `9` for the `E_11` orbit.
3. Test the uncut parent, every pinch class, symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking cuts, bulk
   cells, exceptional guard cells, and a deliberately asymmetrically colored control.
4. Require exact equality of compressed and uncompressed bounded source spans, rules, and terminal
   normal forms. Require zero uncovered branches in any closed artifact.
5. Publish histograms of task-orbit sizes, residual stabilizer orders, orbit seeds, materialized
   rows, nonzeros, pivot fill, wall time, and peak resident memory.

Correctness failure kills the lane. If template storage improves but admitted rows, nonzeros, or
peak memory improve by less than 20% on the S4-stable workload, retain only canonical task caching
and abandon source-orbit elimination. The asymmetric fallback must add less than 10% overhead.

### K10: stabilizer survival test

Use a complete `K = 10` `S5` proxy plus a nine-propagator/one-ISP four-loop vacuum family with one
high-symmetry and one asymmetric decoration. No production four-loop closure is implied.

1. Reproduce the `20`-image, rank-`16` orbit envelope.
2. Run radius-one and radius-two translated-source frames with and without cuts.
3. Measure the fraction of weighted matrix work lying in tasks with nontrivial exact stabilizer.
4. Kill K21 extrapolation if at least 75% of admitted nonzeros occur in trivial-stabilizer tasks, or
   if peak memory improves by less than `1.25x` on the high-symmetry case.

### K15: physical-decoration and rank-transport test

Use the `S6` complete-family proxy and a 12-propagator/three-ISP five-loop vacuum family.

1. Reproduce the `30`-image, rank-`25` source envelope.
2. Run only bounded radius-two and incidence-selected radius-three frames.
3. Probe numerator ranks `8`, `16`, and `32` under every non-permutation ISP action.
4. Require exact replay after any modular block solve and after every route through a guard stratum.
5. Kill the general linear-ISP lane if transport support or memory grows by more than `10x` over
   permutation transport at two successive ranks. Keep the permutation-only fallback.
6. Do not recommend K21 unless admitted nonzeros or peak memory improve by at least `1.5x` on the
   physical high-symmetry workload and the gain survives its principal boundary strata.

### K21: launch condition, not an experiment result

The full `S7` proxy must reproduce one seed, 42 orbit images, rank 36, and rational block dimensions
`1, 6, 14, 15`. This is a control, not evidence for a generic six-loop topology.

Before any genuine K21 completion campaign:

- enumerate every relevant decorated 15-propagator/six-ISP vacuum topology;
- report stabilizer and orbit-seed histograms for its real cells and guards;
- show that source and translated-task quotienting lowers measured nonzeros or fill, not only stored
  generator formulas;
- prove that nonminimal terminals form a finite universal complement; and
- retain a deterministic uncompressed fallback for every trivial or unsupported stratum.

A claim of `36 sources -> 1 source` without the 36-dimensional exact span and full closure replay is
an immediate rejection.

## Priority decision

Implement only the K6 experiment after the currently authorized closure work permits it. The most
valuable product is likely a reusable authenticated task-orbit cache and a stabilizer histogram.
The more ambitious equivariant sparse solver survives only if K6 and K10 show lower matrix fill and
memory. Orbit-seed compression alone is too weak to change the six-loop ranking.

The strongest safe hypothesis is therefore:

> Graph symmetry can reduce repeated discovery and split invariant sparse systems, while exact
> source-span replay preserves all-rank closure. It cannot reduce the mathematical ordinary-source
> rank and it provides no benefit on a trivial decorated stabilizer.

That hypothesis is precise, measurable, and falsifiable before RustRed commits to K21
infrastructure.
